summary: Quarterly readiness workshop to align on usage growth, cost controls, and rollout plan for Sapphire's inference features. Focus on scaling strategy (hosted vs dedicated vs private), autoscaling policies, cost guardrails, and security/KMS questions. Action plan includes pilot SOW, benchmarks, and docs exchange.
topics: KV cache and prefix caching strategies
transcript:
[00:00] Laura (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll go about an hour, keep it practical. Quick intros?
[00:12] Rachel (Sapphire): Rachel here, head of ML. We're focused on rolling to 50k users in Q2.
[00:18] Tom (Sapphire): Tom, infra. I'm here for network and capacity stuff.
[00:21] Priya (Sapphire): Priya, product. Watching rollout and SLOs.
[00:25] Ankit (Sapphire): Ankit, security. I'll focus on compliance and KMS questions.
[00:29] Laura: Great. Samir from Redwood SE will cover performance and benchmarks.
[00:33] Samir (Redwood SE): Hi all. I'll dive into batching, KV cache, and autoscale behavior.
[00:39] Maya (Redwood CSM): Maya, I'll own the adoption timeline and runbooks.
[01:02] Rachel: Quick context — current stack is mixed. We call Redwood hosted for prototypes, but want to shift heavier traffic to either Dedicated or a Private VPC by May. Primary constraints: latency < 250ms p95 on user-facing prompts, and cost budget capped at $35k/mo for inference.
[01:20] Laura: Got it. What's current QPS and token mix?
[01:26] Jared (data eng): We're at ~120 reqs/s peak on staging, production bursts about 200-250 reqs/s after marketing pushes. Average prompt length 120 tokens, responses ~220 tokens.
[01:38] Samir: That mix suggests throughput pressure; batching helps but increases tail latency. We can tune continuous batching windows and priority routes for low-latency prompts.
[01:50] Tom: On the infra side, we're concerned about cross-account VPC peering and egress. If we do Redwood Private, we need a list of ports and CIDRs.
[01:59] Ankit: Also need to understand key management — we require customer-managed KMS and HSM support for keys in-private. SOC2 attestation too.
[02:06] Laura: We can share SOC2 docs and network topology. Redwood Private supports KMS integrations; there's an on-prem option if needed. We'll send specifics.
[02:14] Rachel: Perfect. On costs, do you have guidance for hybrid setups? E.g., hosted API for bursts and dedicated for steady-state.
[02:22] Samir: Yes. Hybrid routing is common: steady traffic on Dedicated which is cost-predictable, bursts routed to hosted instances with fallback. You can set a policy threshold by RPU or latency to move traffic.
[02:35] Priya: How does the routing policy handle KV cache coherence? If part of traffic hits hosted and part Hits dedicated, do you get cache misses?
[02:44] Samir: Good question. There's a prefix/KV caching layer that can be configured to replicate hot prefixes between pools; but cross-pool cache isn't free — there's sync lag and consistency tradeoffs. Usually we recommend warming keys on the dedicated pool before cutover.
[02:58] Tom: That warming step is key. We don't want initial spikes of cost or errors during rollout.
[03:04] Samir: Right. For rollouts we suggest a canary approach: 5% traffic for two hours, validate latencies and token costs, then ramp. We'll provide a runbook.
[03:15] (crosstalk) Jared: ...and smoke tests for KV hits — make sure the prefix is being cached.
[03:20] Laura: Let's talk numbers. Based on 200 req/s and your token mix, Samir, high-level monthly inference cost estimate for hosted-only?
[03:29] Samir: Rough calc: (200 req/s * avg 340 tokens per interaction * 3600s * 24 * 30) / tokens per second... let me give a ballpark — about 1.8B tokens/mo. With current model profile that's roughly $45k–$60k/mo hosted. Dedicated with reserved capacity can drop unit cost by ~30–45% depending on utilization.
[03:53] Rachel: So Dedicated looks necessary to meet our budget. But we still need headroom for marketing spikes.
[03:59] Samir: Exactly — and Dedicated with burst to hosted is the usual pattern. Also consider quantization profiles; we can reduce memory and cost with INT8 in some models, but check quality regressions.
[04:12] Priya: On quality — we need an eval suite. Can Redwood run automated regressions tied to rollouts?
[04:18] Maya: Yes, Redwood Optimize supports eval comparisons and regression alerts. We can integrate your test prompts and automatically block rollouts if quality drops beyond thresholds.
[04:28] Rachel: Good. We have ~200 test prompts for critical flows.
[04:31] Samir: We'll ingest those for the pilot benchmarks.
[04:34] [05:00] Tom: Networking: if we do VPC Private, what's egress behavior? Do we route via customer NAT or Redwood-managed egress?
[05:08] Laura: For Private we support customer-managed NAT with direct peering; also an option for Redwood-managed egress if customers prefer. We'll send topology options.
[05:16] Ankit: For compliance, we need audit logs with per-request metadata and token retention policy options.
[05:23] Laura: Audit logs are standard; retention length is configurable. We'll attach docs and recommended retention for regulated workloads.
[05:30] Samir: Also note per-route tracing hooks for latency breakdowns you can ingest into your tracing systems.
[05:36] Priya: On SSO, we need SCIM + SAML provisioning for multiple teams.
[05:40] Maya: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for RBAC. We'll include the service provider metadata.
[05:47] Rachel: Ok next — pilot scope. We proposed a 6-week hybrid pilot: stage on Dedicated for steady traffic, orchestrate burst to hosted, run benchmarks, validate latency and cost. Success criteria: p95 latency < 250ms, monthly inference spend <= $35k at projected load, zero regressions on top-200 prompts. Thoughts?
[06:09] Samir: Reasonable. Two clarifying points: 1) Are your SLAs strict for the pilot or target? 2) Do you expect stateful sessions (long KV caches per user)?
[06:18] Rachel: SLAs target only, not contractual in pilot. And yes, session affinity for some flows — KV cache lifetime about 10 minutes.
[06:25] Samir: That works. We'll recommend KV cache TTLs and pre-warm strategy in the runbook.
[06:30] [08:00] Tom: For benchmarking, I want to emulate our burst patterns — sudden 5x for 20 minutes. Can Redwood simulate that?
[08:08] Samir: Yes, we'll provide a script. We'll run it with you on staging. We also recommend using realistic user distribution — not uniform.
[08:16] Jared: We'll supply an anonymized sample event trace for spike shaping.
[08:20] Samir: Perfect.
[08:22] [10:00] Priya: On rollout mechanics, can we do blue-green deploys with automatic fallback to previous model or route?
[10:08] Samir: Yes, rollouts support canary and A/B with automatic rollback on errors or quality regressions. You'll map success metrics and rollback thresholds.
[10:17] Rachel: Does rollback preserve KV cache to avoid cold starts?
[10:20] Samir: Cache is separate; rolling back the model will not magically restore the warmed cache unless you replicate prefix entries. We'll note strategies.
[10:28] (brief pause)
[10:40] Ankit: Security question — do you support in-transit encryption with customer-managed certs and mutual TLS between Redwood and customer VPC?
[10:49] Laura: Mutual TLS is supported in private deployments; hosted uses TLS with strict cert validation. For private we can support customer certs/mTLS endpoints.
[10:58] Ankit: And KMS — we need envelope encryption and HSM-backed keys.
[11:03] Samir: Yes, Redwood Private integrates with customer KMS/HSM for key wrapping. We'll send whitepaper.
[11:09] Ankit: Also want to validate retention of logs — we need to redact PII at ingestion if possible.
[11:15] Maya: We have configurable ingestion filters; we can add a PII redaction step before logs are stored. We'll demo that.
[11:22] Rachel: Thanks. On monitoring — we need cost per route and token-level cost breakdowns in console.
[11:28] Laura: Console provides per-route token counts and cost estimates; we can create a dashboard for your top three routes.
[11:34] Priya: We want alerts when cost burn rate exceeds forecast by 15% in a day.
[11:39] Maya: We'll set up cost alerts and an ops playbook for handling overruns.
[11:44] [15:00] (Samir shares screen briefly, reads benchmark plan)
[15:06] Samir: Here's the plan: Week 0 - staging preparation; Week 1 - dedicated capacity provision; Week 2 - canary; Week 3-4 - ramp and validation; Week 5-6 - runbook handoff and go-live.
[15:20] Rachel: That timeline looks good; we'd prefer to start staging prov by 3/19.
[15:26] Tom: Agree, plus we need 48h lead time for peering changes with infra team.
[15:30] Laura: OK we'll aim to have SOW draft by 3/17 and staging provisioning wizardized for 3/19.
[15:36] Jared: About model quantization — will that be a separate rollout with AB tests?
[15:41] Samir: Yes, quantization should be tested as part of canary. We'll run eval suite and compare embeddings/outputs.
[15:48] Priya: Any known model families that regress with INT8 we should avoid?
[15:52] Samir: Large decoder-only sometimes shows subtle regressions under aggressive quant, we'll highlight models with Redwood-verified profiles.
[15:59] [20:00] Rachel: Ok, let's capture the risks: 1) Cost explosion on spikes if routing misconfigured; 2) Cold-start KPI regressions on KV misses; 3) Compliance gating for private deployment.
[20:14] Laura: Good list. Mitigations: autoscale caps, pre-warming scripts, and compliance checklist we'll share.
[20:21] Ankit: Also require a penetration test before go-live.
[20:25] Laura: Noted. We'll coordinate with Security for scope and timeline.
[20:30] Priya: For success metrics during pilot, can we get daily digest emails for p95, token spend, and regression flags?
[20:36] Maya: Yes, we can create a pilot dashboard and daily report.
[20:39] Jared: We'll also want a cost projection model — what happens if monthly traffic doubles.
[20:44] Samir: We'll run sensitivity analysis and include that in the pilot binder.
[20:48] [30:00] (short silence)
[30:10] Rachel: One last product question — can you limit model families per route to avoid drift?
[30:16] Samir: Yes, route policies can pin model families and versions. You can also setup automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant on errors.
[30:24] Priya: Great.
[30:27] Laura: Recap of next steps: Laura to send SOW draft & pricing by 3/17; Samir to send benchmark scripts and schedule 2-hour perf run week of 3/23; Tom to prep staging VPC by 3/19; Ankit to share KMS/HSM requirements by 3/16; Maya to configure pilot dashboard and alerts.
[30:50] Rachel: That matches our expectations. Anything else?
[30:55] Priya: No, thanks.
[30:58] Tom: One small ask — can Redwood share a sample runbook for a canary rollback?
[31:03] Samir: Yes, will attach runbook to SOW email.
[31:08] Laura: Great. We'll follow up after the call. Thanks everyone.
[31:12] (meeting ends)
